title: Sale Ad Creatives With Editable Offers | AIVideosUGC
description: Build a sale ad from one product photo. Type the confirmed price, code, and end date in the editor, then reuse the same scene when the offer changes.
lead: Get a sale video that says the last day out loud, from the product page you already have. An AI avatar holds the item, and you can change the offer line before anyone else sees the file.

faq.q: How many credits does a countdown video cost?
faq.a: A photo spends 24 credits. A video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. You see the cost before you start. If a job fails, those credits come back. A finished file is not refunded just because you dislike it.

faq.q: Can my own software ask for countdown videos?
faq.a: Yes. Your tools can request a sale video from a product link through the API. The file stays in your account until you decide to share it.

faq.q: Can an AI avatar present the sale?
faq.a: Yes. Use the AI avatar from your other clips, so the sale video looks like the same shop.

faq.q: How do I add an offer end time to a sale video?
faq.a: Set the end in the editor, and move it if the sale window shifts. You decide when it stops.

faq.q: What if the product was already filmed on my table?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a product page so the photos come in, upload a picture, or add a clip you already shot. You still check the offer before it goes out.

faq.q: Can I run the same scene on the next offer?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the product scene and swap the line, the voice, or the clock when the code changes.

faq.q: Can I show the earlier price beside the sale price?
faq.a: Only if you really charged that earlier price. Check the rules where you sell before an old price sits next to the new one.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid sale ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark, so you can place it as a paid ad. The app you pick still has its own rules.

faq.q: Can I make sale videos for many products together?
faq.a: Yes. Send several product links and each one comes back as its own ad. Review every file before it is published.

benefits_h2: A Deadline Turns a Sale Into an Event

benefits.t: One AI Avatar for the Sale
benefits.d: One AI avatar carries every clip in this sale, so the jacket ad looks like the same shop as your other videos. Describe the shirt and the hair once, and that face opens the clip by naming the last day.
benefits.alt: Denim jacket on a hanger against a pale wall with open space for an offer.

benefits.t: A Spoken Pitch With the Deadline
benefits.d: You get a spoken pitch from the blanket's page, and the last day lands as the final line. A buyer hears the offer, not a pile of features.
benefits.alt: Adult hands fold a checked picnic blanket beside a basket at a park table.

benefits.t: Slow the Voice on the End Date
benefits.d: A buyer remembers the end date after one scroll when the voice eases on Thursday night. Pick a warm voice, keep the rest of the line quick, and leave the charging pad in the shot.
benefits.alt: Adult hand places a wireless charging pad on a dark desk.

benefits.d: Make two cuts of the tea pouch. One opens on the pack, and the other opens by naming the last day. Keep the file people reply to, and run that one.
benefits.alt: Adult hands prepare a kraft tea pouch beside a plain travel mug in a bright kitchen.

reviews.h2: How Shops Make a Sale Banner for an Online Store
reviews.lead: Three ways a shop leaves room for an offer that is not final yet.

items.t: Leave open space beside the jar
items.d: They paste the product link and ask for a clean counter with empty room on one side. The percent off is typed later, so a changed number does not need a new scene.

items.t: Run the jacket scene again next week
items.d: They keep the same jacket scene and swap the actor's line for the next code. Only the offer text in the editor changes.

items.t: Fold the blanket, then set the timer
items.d: They show the blanket in use and set the end time in the editor once the sale window is real.

trust.h2: Sale Clips a Small Team Can Ship
trust.lead: A small team can ship sale videos from one countdown setup, without a production desk.

items.d: The first seconds carry the deadline and the product, so a viewer gets the offer before the swipe. You can redo that opening without booking another film day.

items.t: A Smaller Bill to Get a Buyer
items.d: What you save on creators can go straight to reach, since each job draws from the credit balance you already have.

items.t: A Full Slate of Sale Clips
items.d: Once the look is chosen, you can make countdown videos across the catalog instead of waiting on one editor.

items.t: Sale Clips Without a Shoot Day
items.d: A product page and a few choices stand in for a location day, a talent call, and an edit queue.

items.t: A New Test Whenever the Code Changes
items.d: Try another opening or another voice when the offer changes. You are not stuck with one sale video for the whole month.
You can brief, generate, and export the weekend countdown set after the orders are packed. One person can cover it, so nobody else has to stay.
